title: One .env file, two jobs
subtitle: Compose reads .env itself to fill in ${...}. env_file: hands the same lines to the app inside the container.

nodes.label: docker compose up
nodes.detail:
1. reads .env by itself
2. fills in ${WEB_PORT} → 4000
3. starts the container

nodes.label: greet-web-1
nodes.detail:
app.js reads
process.env.NAME → Tanvi
process.env.COLOR → pink
listens on 3000

edges.label:
job 1: env_file
NAME, COLOR
→ the app

notes.text:
Job 2 always happens: Compose looks for .env in the folder you run it from, with or without env_file.

Job 1 only happens with env_file: .env. Without it, the app gets nothing from the file.

Who wins for ${...}: the terminal (WEB_PORT=5000 docker compose up), then .env, then the default after :-

docker compose config
# shows the file with every ${...} filled in
WEB_PORT=5000 docker compose up -d
# the terminal beats .env
